To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Finite State Machine based controller for ECU demand response in a hybrid microgrid can significantly reduce the amount of fuel used in a SIP structure while maintaining a comfortable temperature range.

we developed a novel Finite State Machine based controller for the environmental control system of a microgrid that leverages thermal energy storage in the structure to improve the coupling of the environmental control system to PV production and improve the performance of the microgrid.

a FSM based controller for ECU systems in hybrid military microgrids is able to reduce diesel generator run times, reduce the number of generator starts, and reduce the number of times the ECU system is cycled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a novel, FSM, based control system for ECU in hybrid diesel generator/photovoltaic microgrids.
the control of the ECU system and how to best couple the energy demand of the system to the energy production of a hybrid diesel generator/Pv microgrid.
developing and implementing a novel, FSM controller for the ECUs in hybrid diesel generator/Photovoltaic (PV)/Battery microgrids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a novel, FSM-based controller was developed for the ECU system in hybrid microgrids.

this work has developed a new controller that leverages the thermal mass of the SIP structures as energy storage, which can improve the performance of hybrid military microgrids with a PV asset and a battery storage system.
the FSM based control of ECU energy demand can significantly improve energy storage and energy management in hybrid diesel generator based microgrid systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed FSM based DR controller for ECU in hybrid diesel generator/ PV microgrids is ready for implementation.

a novel FSM based controller has been developed to handle intraday PV variability and improve coupling of ECU energy demand with PV energy production while still maintaining a comfortable environment in a hybrid diesel generator/Pv microgrid.

the FSM based controller has the potential to significantly improve the coupling of ECU load demand to PV energy generation in a hybrid microgrid, and the FSM based controller is ready for implementation in a microgrid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECU system is an excellent resource for energy storage in a military microgrid.
a novel FSM based control algorithm can significantly improve the performance of hybrid microgrids with PV and ECU loads.
a FSM based controller for ECU can improve the energy balance in hybrid microgrids and reduce the need for energy storage, thus reducing costs and risk.
